utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I should say at the outset, in light of Judge Kwon's unavoidable absence, Judge Bonomy and I sit pursuant to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. Mr. Caric.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see you have come armed with assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARIC
utterances.text: Yes. On my left side is Mr. Igor Oljuic. Igor Oljuic is legal counsellor. Second on my left side is Mr. Svetislav Rabrenovic. He is a counsellor in the National Council for Cooperation with the Tribunal. Today we represent the government of Serbia and Montenegro in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I have nothing to add save to say that the translation service has provided bundles of papers in translation, each bundle an excerpt from one of the various files, and the selection being made according to the pages identified by Serbia and Montenegro. I see we are in open session. I assume that's what the applicant wants, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are in open session at the outset, but I think for the purposes of the hearing from Serbia and Montenegro we would be in closed session, I presume. Yes, in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Nice: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last week we diverted from chronological exploration of what happened scene by scene to ask you some questions about your colleagues all writing statements that indicated the book "As Seen, As Told" had been written by or produced by Natasa Kandic. You didn't offer an explanation for how it could be that those statements could all make the same mistake. Have you been able to think about that any more?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I personally am concerned, the contents of the book for the most part it seems that the book was published by the Humanitarian Law Fund headed, as far as I know, by Natasa Kandic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who you all dislike because she forces Serbs to confront their own history, doesn't she? She brooks no denial.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my personal attitude to Ms. Kandic is irrelevant here. I don't know the lady. I have never met her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you have produced statements, and it's you who is producing these statements, from your colleagues that express strong, virulent views on her, saying they're disgusted by her and that's why they didn't read the book. You've chosen to produce that material. Am I not right that Natasa Kandic is loathed by the Serbs because she forces them to confront their own history when they would rather avoid it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are wrong. You're asking me to tell you what all Serbs think. I can only tell you what I think. I can only be held responsible for what I think and say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Nort, please. If you would be good enough to take my copy of "As Seen, As Told" and just lay it on the overhead projector. Your Honours will appreciate I observed yesterday -- last week that we didn't have the Serbian version, and we still don't. My understanding is it was simply translated. This is in English. Mr. Nort, stay by the machine, please, and we'll turn over a few pages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at the first page in English, it says: "An analysis of the human rights findings of the OSCE Kosovo Verification Mission."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Next page, please, Mr. Nort. End of the contents. Pass over from the contents, please. Then there's an introduction. "This report is the outcome of the tireless efforts of many people committed to the cause of human rights and justice. First, the women and men of the OSCE Kosovo Verification Mission, and so on. Next page, please. Executive Summary. Pass on beyond the Executive Summary, please. Turn over a few pages. Get to the end of the Executive Summary, please. Just keep going. Turn it over. Keep going, keep going. And then Introduction. We'll stop at the Introduction. "In developing this report, the analytical methodologically and reporting strategy applied by the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights was driven by the data collection of the OSCE Kosovo Verification Mission."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in English that's the opening pages of this document. You've said in your statements you read it, thinking it was written by Natasa Kandic. Please tell us, did you actually read it or did somebody else draft these statements for you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, what you're saying is absolutely ridiculous. The book that I read is not this book. The cover is quite different. It's red. And I read the book, especially the parts relating to my area and also parts relating to other areas in Kosovo and Metohija. Let me just see if it's organised by region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Well --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The book is organised by region, more or less, but the cover of the book I read is quite different; and as for the beginning, I'm not sure it was the same. What is important is that I read everything that relates to my area, and each of my commanding officers read it as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Therefore, your statement that it was somebody else who wrote these statements or that people did not read this book is absolutely untrue. We did not have many copies of the book, so each officer asked to photocopy that part of the book which relates to his area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that was possible while I still had my copy of the book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, this, because we need to understand the fairness, the objectivity, the neutrality of the process whereby those of you sitting round the table, as you've described, prepared statements. Who was it amongst your number who explained that this book was Natasa Kandic's work? Somebody must have done it, mustn't they? Who did that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the book was published by the Fund for Humanitarian Law, people drew their own conclusions. I never put it into anyone's mouth that it was Natasa Kandic's book, but it was the Humanitarian Law Fund that had the book translated and published.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... another topic. You've produced as part of your materials that you ask the -- that the accused asked through you that the Court should rely on, a number of clips from RTS, and you will recall that when I raised queries --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- questions about the journalists concerned, you were able to name them without any further reference. How, if at all, are you able to vouch for the reliability of the RTS material?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can guarantee for these materials a hundred per cent, because they were made in my area --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me explain what I mean a little bit more by "vouch." Let's break it down. Were you present with the journalists when they conducted the interviews that we have seen?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've told you: Every time when I was present you could actually see me in some of these material, that I was there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've seen a lot of material and we'd like to know. You tell us which ones you were present at, because sometimes you won't be seen by the camera. Which ones were you present at?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present, and you can see me in the footage with the verifiers at Krbos, which was on the 3rd or 4th of December. I was present on the 14th of December, also in 1998, then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We won't necessarily be able to remember the place names, but I'm sure the Judges and I would all readily remember the images. Some of them are quite memorable, like the trench diggers and others. You tell us which ones you were present at because you'll remember.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember. I was present when the column was targeted. I was there on the spot. I was present at Pastrik when that large quantity of weapons was found. I was present a few days before that at Pastrik again when a smaller quantity of weapons was found and when eight terrorists were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any others? What about the trench digging?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the trench diggers. Were you present there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or the village of Zjum. Were you present there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. It's not the job of a brigade commander to accompany a TV crew. But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You might have been there. You were often at the front line. Forgive my asking you the question. There was another one as well, I think, wasn't there, one of a mother and her daughter. It was the mother talking, actually, but we saw a daughter or son standing there. Were you present at that one?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take the ones where you weren't present, Mr. Delic, and you tell us how you can vouch for those, because you're presenting that as evidence on which this Chamber can rely. You tell us why we should rely on that material.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I brought the video footage that was filmed by the TV studio in Prizren. I know the editor who was always present. I know the cameraman who was always present too. The editor's name is Borivoje Ugrinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this day he works at TV --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your account that Mr. Ugrinovic was present at all of these clips? And I have in mind the woman and her daughter, the trench diggers, and the video involving the doctor. Think back and be careful with your answers, please. Was Mr. Ugrinovic present at all of these?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The footage should be played because his voice can be heard very often, but without him there could be no filming. I think he was present at all the filmings. He was present whenever I was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we're now dealing with the ones where you weren't present. Now, the other journalist you say was present apart from Mr. Ugrinovic was who?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sanjevic was the other journalist. I cannot remember his first name. To this day he is employed in Radio-Television Serbia but in Belgrade, whereas Ugrinovic is in Radio-Television Serbia but in Nis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Radio-Television Serbia was a loathed television programme by many people, wasn't it, because it put out hate on behalf of this accused throughout these unhappy events; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's just your opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were many programmes after the downfall of this accused setting out how RTS had been used as a wicked weapon of propaganda; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, Radio-Television Serbia is a professional institution. It has a very rich professional history. So professionals cannot allow any politician --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to jeopardise their professional integrity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that so well, General as you are?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I certainly know it better than you do because I watched that television, and also from time to time I had the opportunity to watch CNN or the BBC. During the war, it is certain that this radio television reported more truthfully than CNN did or Jamie O'Shea as the NATO spokesperson. After all, that TV was bombed, and all its repeaters throughout the country, so it would not disseminate the truth rather than lies, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, your judgement of RTS, is that informed by your watching the programmes that followed the downfall of the accused which described it as an instrument of hate, or did you not bother to watch these programmes?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, you'll find them mentioned extensively in Mr. de la Brosse's report.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I watched television before and afterwards. Others came, different people who support different political views, but after all, every person has his own views. I think that to this day Radio-Television Serbia reports professionally about everything that goes on in the country, as it did earlier too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few more general points about RTS and the media of communication generally. It's right, isn't it, that shortly after the start of NATO bombing a noted journalist, Slavko Caruvija, was assassinated for no reason whatsoever, in the company of his wife as he was at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes but I didn't have that information at that time, but later on a lot was written in the country about that journalist and his killing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was killed by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems that you know this better than the MUP in Serbia does. It hasn't been proven and his killer has not been found yet, at least not while I was still in Belgrade. These are insinuations on your part fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No other candidate for the killing of Slavko Caruvija but the MUP of Serbia, is there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are absolutely presenting inaccuracies. The MUP of Serbia is working on solving this case, especially now, this MUP that you are talking about that changed after the departure of this accused person, after he was no longer in power. Had there been additional information about this, we would have known about it, we in that country. We are certainly more interested in that than you are. This is yet another unresolved murder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Koha Ditore, the Albanian language newspaper, was compelled to stop printing on the 23rd of March, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a fact that I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Albanian newspapers -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of the staged appearance on RTS between Ibrahim Rugova and this accused? Do you remember that happening when you were in Kosovo? You will have had an interest in it.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have to give me the date when this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards the end of the period of the bombing, but this is the way -- I haven't got the exact date and I'm not even sure that Mr. Rugova gave us the exact date, but this is the way paragraph 99 of the expert's report on propaganda, that it's expressed: "He was taken from his monitored residence in Pristina and the main purpose for this strange and surrealistic meeting was to make people believe that the Serbs wanted to relaunch negotiations at a time when ethnic cleansing in the field was increasing." Is it right as I suggest to you -- well, first of all, did you see on television a broadcast of this meeting between Ibrahim Rugova and this accused?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no one could see that broadcast because you destroyed all our repeaters. NATO destroyed all our repeaters. I know from later on that this meeting had actually taken place, but Ibrahim Rugova is alive today precisely because during the war he was provided with security by the security forces. Otherwise, the KLA would have killed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, and I'll come back to the press and television tomorrow, but the reality is that you were operating - you the army - in a police state which was supported by a propaganda machine, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are completely wrong, and you are terribly ignorant of the situation in our country, and if you wish I can prove that to you, because you're just telling stories, and I am saying let's look at what the evidence is. Let us see what papers say, what documents say, and you certainly don't want to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should ask you, because you've had some time to think about last week's questions and I must do it before I forget: Have you brought any further papers with you or have you unearthed from wherever you're staying any further papers contemporaneous with these events that you're going to say are relevant to the matters we're inquiring into?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depends on the questions that you put. I certainly have, if I can put it this way, hundreds of answers to your questions, and I also have the required number of documents too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've been asking you about this since you started answering my questions: Have you now got the war diary with you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I used my documentation when you mention a certain period or a certain event, because I don't want to engage in empty talk here. I want to corroborate things I want to support my own answers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... war diary with you? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have my war diary with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the war diary we've been seeking, for how many years is it? Two or three, I can't remember. Where was it last week, for example? Was it in your hotel room? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My war diary was always with me, and you see it's always here, right by me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What period does it cover?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it's not necessary for me to explain the same thing to you ten times. If one says "war diary," it covers the war, period. Everyone knows when the war started and when it ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other documents have you got that are contemporaneous apart from that? You described it, I think, actually differently from "war diary" last time, but I might be wrong. What other documents have you got that are contemporaneous? You see, my recollection, and it may be Mr. Coo's and the Court's is the same, that last week you told us about your possession here of a personal notebook. You didn't tell us that you had your brigade's formal war diary. Which is the document you've got here?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I said that I had a notebook, then this is it. That's where I started taking notes in the hotel over here before I started giving testimony. I've already said it's no secret. I said that on day one, and you can have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I have a look at the war diary, please? Well, the document you've now described as the war diary, may I please see it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you like to take it out of your briefcase and hand it over. We'll have it looked at. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness produces a bound photocopied document written in Cyrillic covering the period 24th of March and until -- at the moment I can't find the last date, but as the witness isn't using it, with his leave and the Court's leave, I'll keep it on the Prosecution's bench against -- so that I can refer to it or refer him to it. We'll deal with its destination perhaps at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When that document was prepared, copied --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just say something. You do not have my permission. After all, let the Trial Chamber decide on this. I brought this document for other purposes; if the Defence requests it. So you can take this document and the Trial Chamber can so decide, but without my permission. That is to say, you can take it by force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... this. You brought a prepared, copied, nicely bound document that contains what you tell us is a contemporaneous record of yours, but you were only prepared to make it available to the Defence, not voluntarily to the Court or the Prosecution. Is that really your position?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So far we did not touch upon my war diary in a single word or a single sentence. First of all, you don't understand what a war diary is. These are not my own notes. First of all, these are not my own notes. These are notes of the officer who kept the war diary, and in a certain period of time during a particular day was the duty officer by the telephone. I did not enter a single word in that diary by myself personally. It is a war diary of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, where last week you appeared to be talking about a personal notebook that covered the same period, may I have a look at that, please?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not got a personal notebook that covers that period, and I never said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. My last question on the RTS, to which we'll return tomorrow, is that - you must correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Delic - you present the material from RTS on the basis that these journalists whom you know are of such integrity that anything they produce must be reliable. Would that be a fair summary of what you're seeking to explain to the Court?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. These are very professional and responsible persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's now look at another question, but as we come to it, you do understand, don't you, that the material you're presenting, statements of your subordinate officers, statements of people being interviewed, and documents all have to have about them integrity. That is, they have to be clearly documents that the Court can rely on. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we now turn briefly to documents, perhaps you'd take what in the English version is binder 6, and it's tab 444. Before we look at it -- by all means open it, open it, and then I'll come to my question with one preparatory question for you. You have shown us, have you not, by various entries in various documents, that you were able to report or --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the tab number you said?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 444. Now, before we look at the document, you can confirm, really, that your reporting system, up to you and then from you up to the Pristina Corps, enabled a very full picture of any event on the ground to be logged, recorded, and transmitted, would that be correct? Any important event on the ground.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed it was your duty, you, perhaps to some degree collectively with the police, but it was your duty to record things that affected the security position of Kosovo at that time. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm responsible for my area. When I report to my superior, I report about my own zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's only because, although we haven't seen the underlying material, that there's a wealth of such material that you and your subordinate officers, were able to prepare these various statements explaining what you say happened in the matters complained of in the indictment against this accused.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When these materials were elaborated, they were made in accordance with what the National Commission for Cooperation with the ICTY requested it. This accused is not aware of it nor anybody else. This was done in order to elucidate certain events that are referred to in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then let's turn our attention, if we may, Mr. Delic, to the question of population movement. If you look at this document, which comes from your materials, the 30th of March, a few days after things started, we see this from Lazarevic, under Order, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What tab is that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an order. That's not Lazarevic's document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hope so. There we are. "I hereby order: "Enable free passage for the entire population leaving the threatened areas on the exit axes from Kosovo and Metohija towards the Republic of Albania and Macedonia." Now, this is a reference to the movement of refugees, and it says basically let them out. Do you remember that order?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember that order. It's right here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Its effect is to say let them go, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is referred to here are the measures that units should take in order to protect this population and to make it possible for them to go in the direction where they wished to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just let them go in the direction they wish to go, is it? Now, I'd like you to look at another document. One of the things -- you're not a policeman, Mr. Delic, but one of the things about people who commit crime is that in laying -- in covering their tracks they sometimes forget to set out what they would do if they were innocent. Shall we look at this document, please. This is dated the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Coming your way, Your Honours. Your Honours, this is a new document provided by the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a document from Pavkovic. You didn't produce it, but never mind. It's dated the 20th of April. Take your time to review it. We'll only look at one part of it at the moment, maybe two. It describes the enemy for the period of 19th to the 20th of April, and now this document of the 20th of April, three paragraphs in, says: "There are 6.000 to 8.000 members of the so-called KLA in north-west Macedonia..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it I think also deal elsewhere with the movement of individuals, or is that it? No. It deals with NATO forces in the paragraph before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just give me one minute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then if you go over the page, under 2, just towards the top, Mr. Nort, it says: "On the 19th and 20th of April, through the area of the 3rd Battalion of the 78th Motorised Brigade... around 3.000 people left the territory escorted and organised by the Presevo MUP." So here's an order, or a report, rather, and this time it's from Pavkovic, I think, detailing 3.000 people. Keep the document with you for another reason, but I just --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't found that portion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's under -- it's under 2, and then you go to 2.1, and it's under the 19th and 20th of April. All right? See it there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to look at this document for one other reason, so just keep it by you. But help me with this, please: Where else can we find in all your documentation reference to the plight of, the problem of, or the number of refugees?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are many documents regulating the relationship of the army towards refugees, the attitude of the army, and a similar order as written by General Lazarevic is one that on the basis of his order I wrote myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Where do we find reference to their numbers, their plight, and how to deal with them? We saw Pavkovic's order, which is let them go. These are your fellow countrymen. Where do we find --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my area, in my zone, there -- they didn't have any particular problems, so if any medical assistance was needed, it was provided. Pursuant to General Pavkovic's order, they saw whether the population leaving had enough food, and the conclusion was that they did have enough food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do we find the documents discussing whether they should be encouraged or discouraged, how they should be helped, where they should be sent, why they should be sent through narrow funnels created by mines to the south-west and not back to areas where it might be safer for them to stay? Where do we find that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in various documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are your documents, all eight binders of them, and of course we may have missed something, but were there any documents, contemporaneous documents, that dealt with the plight of the refugees?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The refugees were not the army's problem. They were the problem of the civilian authorities which functioned, and the refugees just passed through the zone under army control, and it was up to the army to provide --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No need, no duty on you to record the thousands of refugees escorted by your officers off the premises, as it were? No need to record that, Mr. Delic, or is the truth that because you wanted them to go you didn't want to record their --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you. It's not my opinion. I don't have an opinion. I'm here to ask questions, and I want you to tell us, please. We may have missed the documents. It may be in your war diary. Well -- what are you looking at now, please?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, indeed you do not have your opinion, but very often you speak off the top of your head. I'm looking at the war diary of my commander who was at the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another contemporaneous document that you have produced from your bag that we haven't seen that would have been covered by one of our requests. What period does it cover?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document does not come under your request for assistance. It is a battalion document. And since you asked me some things now, may we place this on the overhead projector and read it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not immediately because I'm still asking questions, and it's not, I think, responsive -- well, it may be responsive, I suppose, but better tell me what it covers first and then we'll see if we're going to look at it. What does it cover and what is it? What does it cover?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war diary of my commander, and along that axis there was a border crossing, and he recorded who was leaving, how many refugees were leaving on what day, what the problems they were having were, and what the army was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Uh-huh. We'd like to have a look at that in a minute. Have you got any other war diaries of battalion commanders in your bag?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go above your battalion commander to your level. Why is it that your documents don't record the plight and the problems and the numbers of the refugees, for you as a senior army officer reporting to the Pristina command owed a duty to inform them of what was happening.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly does. Problems that NATO had bombed the refugees and what the unit did. So all of that is recorded in those diaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you recall no other document, is that the position, that deals with the plight of the refugees? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember every document, and there are documents which write about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the one that you may temporarily have forgotten. 474, please, in binder 7. If you'd like to find that. Do you remember my earlier questions a few minutes ago about the necessary integrity of documents, radio broadcasts, and the statements of your colleagues? Do you remember what I asked you about that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... ask you questions about the integrity of this document which you don't seem to have remembered, but let's have a look at it. It's dated the 3rd of April, 1999, just a week after the start of the bombing. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then without looking at it any further, tell us why did you prepare it, for whom, and what was its purpose?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document speaks about the situation in the area of responsibility and was sent to the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at the top of the document, shall we? It's got a reference number in hand, 1334-3. Yes? Can you explain to us the numbering system, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the document is recorded in the office, then it receives the next number in line in the logbook, the next number in line, and this logbook is kept in the brigade office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, one of the problems about creating a false document, if this were ever to have been done, is that you'd need to be able to give it an apparently genuine number, wouldn't you, because otherwise there's always a chance people will be given access to a logbook and be able to look for the preceding and the immediate following document.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This logbook is kept for a period of one year, so this is the 1999 logbook, and it goes up to the end of 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that the documents are sequential, which number changes? Is the number -- is the document before 1334-3, 1333-3, or is it 1334-2?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: In front of this 1334-2, 1334-1. Those are the ones in front, before. So that would be the order, the sequence. And after this, perhaps it was 1334-4 or perhaps a new number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what does 1334 mean, in case we ever need to pursue this further?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1334 is that number in the logbook. The previous number was 1334, that number of documents. So at the beginning of the year, from January, starting with January, we start with number 1. That's the first number in the sequence, on the 1st of January, which means that before this particular document there were more than 1.334 other various documents, orders, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... understand why it's broken down. It could easily have been just numbered 1334, 1335, 1336. Why have we gone through a sequence of 1334 apparently 1 to 3? Just help us with it. It's your system, so we've got to do our best to understand it with your answers, you see?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This would be it: If you receive a document from the Pristina Corps, for example, which, for example, has to do with this situation, then the document, if it is under 1334-1, recorded in that way, then the next document could be a response or reply, and that would be 1334-2, for example. Or if there was an addition, an attachment, it would also be 1334-3. So you can give one number to all the documents in -- on one subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this certainly isn't a reply. It's not even sent to anyone. It's just been created for some reason for the record, hadn't it? It's sent to somebody at the end, but it's not addressed to anyone. Delivered to the commander of the Pristina Corps and the archives. You see -- but it's not actually addressed to anyone. Let's just have a look at it. 290.000 people crossed the border at Vrbnica, plus another 20.000 to 25.000 at Cafa Prusit, and then this: "The very incidence of refugees, especially in that number, came as a surprise." Why did you write that when it was completely untrue?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean that it was untrue?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Remember we went through your Ph.D. thesis and saw at several places how refugees were an absolute inevitability of situations like this? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all wars refugees are an inevitability. The only thing is that it was a surprise that these refugees took off for Albania. There were refugees in 1998 as well, but they were internally displaced persons or, rather, they remained on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, apart from what you said in your thesis, you said the same thing last week. In every war, regardless of where it's going on, there are refugees. And you'll remember that we saw records of refugees from international organisations going back to 1998. And what you wrote was "The very incidence of refugees ... came as a surprise." Why?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't read it correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I read it fully --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The phenomenon of refugees themselves in that number, in that large number, was a surprise. That was the surprise. So don't just read a half a sentence. Read the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delic --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the surprise was that long enormous columns of refugees should appear quite suddenly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, it is a technical point in one sense. I read the sentence quite fully to you the first time and I read it to you in extract intentionally the second time because the sense of your sentence is "The very incidence of refugees came as a surprise." Was this a document by which, whenever it was written, you were trying to cover your tracks of irresponsibility for refugees?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to my irresponsibility or responsibility was something that my superiors decided about. All you're stating is your own opinion. So I was completely responsible towards the refugees because not a single inhabitant leaving Kosovo and Metohija was killed while he was in my area of responsibility. All of them left the area safely and went in the direction they desired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is a letter like this prepared? Did you dictate? Did you do your own word processing? Did somebody draft it for you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you turn to page 2, then you can see that it's not the commanders, you know, who type out documents. That's not their job. But anyway, you can see that this was typed out by a typist of the brigade and her name was Vera Veljanovski. You can see that at the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did she type it to your dictation or did she type it to a handwritten draft, or what?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably it was -- she typed out what I had written in my own handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is she a good typist?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was an excellent typist, and we refer to typists like that as first-class typists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we see how in that first paragraph, if you'll return to it, that you deal with the ever greater numbers coming from remote parts of Kosovo, how they were allowed to enter Albania unhindered, whereafter they were refused entry into Macedonia, and then into Albania, huge numbers standing on the road. You then say: "At our insistence, only a small number of persons returned to their place of residence." Could you just read that sentence in the original Serbian, and if we could have it translated, interpreted. There's a potential ambiguity in it. Could you just read that sentence for us, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At our insistence, only a smaller number of persons returned to their place of residence."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Are you saying that you insisted that they return generally but only a small number of them did, or are you saying that it was your dictate, your order that only a small number went back? It's not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite clear: At our insistence a smaller number of individuals returned to their place of residence. The rest waited for them to -- waited to receive permission to go to the Republic of Albania, and this break lasted two or three days when entry into Albania was interrupted, and it was interrupted on the Albanian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at the subparagraphs under the next paragraph, where you say, based on your talks, the following conclusions could be made. Why so swiftly after the start of the NATO bombing were you conducting a questionnaire or questioning these people?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not compile any kind of questionnaire. It was just talking to people quite freely who were leaving the country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any record of the conversations with these people? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no record because I had these conversations directly. So there was no need for me to keep any records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Everything in this document comes from your own discussions with people at various exit routes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With people, with the police, with the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not just with the refugees. Because you see, under A we have "fear of major fighting between our forces, the KLA and NATO..." And then the last sentence: "In response to our offer to go to Serbia they say that it is realistic to expect a less than warm welcome there," and then this, "because it is their fellow countrymen who have caused the war." Are we to take it from this that Kosovo Albanians leaving Kosovo said to you, "It's all our fellow countrymen's fault, and therefore we think it would be dangerous for us to go to Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They probably thought along the lines that they stated, and there was this offer that they shouldn't go to Albania but to go to Serbia. So, yes, part of them said that, put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these are all your personal conversations, are they?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all based on my personal conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just out of a matter of interest, why did you say "based on the talks we had"?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, this was based on my own conversations, but I also talked to members of the MUP, as I've already said, and with the local authorities as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's move on because this document, I must suggest to you -- well, let's have a look at it a little bit further. Then you say B, they're leaving to avoid forced mobilisation into the KLA ranks. You then observe under B a low number of young men. C, you say a large number of refugees say they fear Arkan's troops but this is probably KLA psychological propaganda. Why did you say that? Wasn't Arkan there or weren't Arkan's troops there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw a single member of this -- these Arkan's troops there, and since 1998 the Albanians kept mentioning Arkan's troops or army, whereas in my area of responsibility there was never a single member of that army or those troops. I didn't see them, nor would I allow them to be in my area of responsibility. And this was certainly psychological warfare which already in 1998 was geared towards this kind of thing, to have villagers join up with the Kosovo Liberation Army because they -- fear was instilled in them about Arkan's troops, and there's a document testifying to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And fearing of NATO bombing, subparagraph D, and then they go on to say "Although there may not have been many strikes on civilian targets in these first days, mostly military, we believe that the fear is realistic, though perhaps not to the extent to which the Siptars emphasise it." You then deal with carrying sufficient supplies of food, flour and oil, and then you say this: "The attitude of the police and army to the persons in the columns was generally proper. According to the reports of commanding officers and the MUP, a small number of VJ troops tried to take property away from refugees ... All such cases were efficiently dealt with, so that eight persons ... were disciplined." What I'm interested to know, Mr. Delic, is why in the crisis that you were facing, when you'd shown so little interest in recording anything about refugees throughout 1998 and 1999, you suddenly wrote this down, as you will tell us, on the 3rd of April. You see, you couldn't have had the indictment that identified what the army had done by then. Hardly time for you to pick up international complaint of what you'd done by then. So tell us, why did you write this down?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These details speak to the fact that the army was efficient in working against all those who violated regulations and who had engaged in some unauthorised activities vis-a-vis people in the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you write this down? It's not sent anywhere. It's sent somewhere but it's not addressed to anyone so that we can't find someone who can say he received it or he requested the report. You say it's in the course of the series, but we don't have the rest of the series. Why did you write it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can you say that it wasn't addressed to anyone, sent to anyone? It was addressed to the Pristina Corps command, the people it was supposed to be addressed to; the superior command, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In reply to a request from them?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no special request. There was just interest on the part of the corps commander via the telephone as to what the situation with the refugees was and whether they needed any assistance. As to the question of why measures taken were reported on or, rather, the errors committed by certain soldiers, that is the most important question which the corps command was interested in. They were most interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, let's look at the last page, paragraph 3, where you set out problems that have occurred: Making available personnel for work in communal services, "... interesting to note the views of local self-administration on why Siptars are leaving... In addition to the reasons we've stated, we underline the following: "They're leaving the country in line with the pre-arranged scenario of 'humanitarian catastrophe' in order to justify the bombing and aggression." Where did you get that from?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says everything in the previous portion. I said that it was interesting to note the views of the bodies of local self-government, for example, on the reasons why Siptars were leaving for Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you get this information from about a pre-arranged scenario of humanitarian catastrophe? Or the next bit, "Siptars are leaving and abandoning the territory so that 'NATO alliance' can bomb all targets indiscriminately ..."? Where did you get that from?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, you're reading the questions but you're not reading the introduction. It says: "It is interesting to note the views of the bodies of local self-administration ..." That means people from the local authorities to whom I spoke about this question, discussed the issue. They were people, Serbs and other ethnicities as well, which I contacted, and I was in contact, daily contact with them, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see if we then turn, if we look at the next part of the document, from all this material to something totally different. "We are of the view that, in the coming period, the following needs to be done to resist the NATO aggression successfully. "Reinforce the units in the border belt ... Speed up the works on the mounting of obstacles ... In as short a time as possible, smash STS in the territory... You need to reinforce us with unit of anti-aircraft capability..." and so on. Do you see that? A complete change of topic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a completely new point. These are problems I raise which existed in my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... curiously -- I don't know if you can help us with this: Rather curiously, your first-class secretary who on paragraph 1 used subparagraphs A to whatever it was, D, in subparagraph 3 appears suddenly and inexplicably to have changed her subparagraph numbering system to 1 and 2, which had the consequence that the last paragraph was originally numbered 3 and then had to be corrected in hand to 4 to make sense of the document. So at exactly the same point in the document as the topic suddenly changes from refugees, the format changes. Is this document --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This numbering and what is written here in ballpoint pen was done by me. The typist wrote what I told her to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, isn't this document which covers, as it were, or provides a defence for the actions of the army at a time when the international community knew and was able to evidence the refugee flow, isn't this documentation part of a cover-up, whenever it was written?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document reflects very realistically the situation in the period it refers to, and it has nothing to do with what you are saying. It mentions the number of refugees based on data received from the MUP, because it was not my job to count the refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as I'm reminded, neither your job to count them nor to interview them, was it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you think, that it was not my job. You say you have no feelings about this. I had feelings about those people. I saved hundreds of people. I saved --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the lives of people in the columns bombed by NATO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. How did you do that? By funneling them through places where there were mines on either side rather than directing them back to areas where people were living in safety, perhaps to the east? Why did you drive them out to the west?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody drove them there. You're talking about driving them out. I'm talking about a scenario that was created outside my country. You are trying to find proof of that scenario, or you're saying that the evidence is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you save them from the bombs of NATO?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were killed could not be saved, but those who had been wounded were all given assistance in my field hospital. No distinction was made. We even organised supplies of blood to save those people. You could have seen this on the videos but evidently that's not what you're interested in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back, then, now. Now, I must deal with crime scenes as quickly as I can. I don't know what time the Court looks to rise in the afternoon sessions. Can we go back to tab 356.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Another ten minutes to the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think we've looked at 356 before. Perhaps we'll look at it now briefly.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have looked at it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Joint Command that shows itself to come from the army. When we look at Orahovac and thereabouts, and Celine, in summary -- I want to deal with these things comparatively quickly -- your grounds for saying that events in Celine -- the Chamber will have the aide-memoire if it finds it helpful - and you'll see Celine identified, but I think you'll find that part of the material is dealt with also in witnesses who deal with Orahovac although it's a little bit further to the north. Your grounds for saying that Celine evidence is incorrect is what, please, Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that everything that the witnesses say about Celine is untrue; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have to say what your witnesses say one by one, or give it to me in the Serbian version so I can read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will recall that the accused took you through some of this and you understand quite well that it's not possible to go through all of it in detail in cross-examination, but the suggestion from a witness, K25, is that you surrounded the village on the night of the 24th of March with tanks and Pragas. Now, K25 is supported by a man called Agim and a man called Isuf Jemini. It's also covered in "As Seen, As Told" and "Under Orders." Can you point to any reason why these people should have made this account up against you and your forces?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not invent anything against me. They don't even mention me. But if you go back to this document which you first offered, tab 356 or 357 or the analysis in 359, you will see that this is absolutely incorrect, that on the 24th of March there were no troops in that area. I know that some kind of black uniforms were mentioned, long knives, and all sorts of things, and this is absolutely untrue. The operations here began on the 25th. On the 24th, there was nothing happening in that location, so that everybody who says something was happening on the 24th are either not telling the truth or they simply don't remember, they are mistaken about the date. But I have a document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll come to have a look at the document in a minute if it's other than the ones we've looked at already. The 25th of March it's been said as against your forces that the shelling began at 6.00 in the morning, lasted until 8.00, a Praga firing continuously towards the village during the day, with your forces in conjunction with the police entering the village, as you say, in black uniforms, tanks, and armoured vehicles around. Now, that evidence has come from witnesses who have been called from Isuf Jemini and Reshit Salihi. There's other material available to like effect. Can you explain why these people could conceivably be mistaken in what they've said?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they're talking about constant shelling, I can say nothing else but that they are not telling the truth, because it is absolutely untrue. Had they said that the Pragas were there on the asphalt road all day but not fired, that would probably have been true. But the reason they are saying this is something I'm not aware of. That's their problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to identify narrowly the issues between you and the witnesses, yes, the heavy weaponry was there, but when they say it was used, completely untrue; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Weapons were used only for firing points according to the rules, not to shell villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we have the burning of the houses, including the mosque, and the robbing and the looting. That comes from many witnesses; Agim Zeqiri, Jemini, Reshit Salihi, Sabri Popaj, and so on. And many other statements are available. But you're saying these people are all making it up?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're reading something about witnesses here. I want you to tell me what each witness said and what was stolen. I'm telling you that my troops did not loot from anyone. These were regular soldiers carrying only their combat kits, only their ammunition and their daily ration and their First Aid kit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the man Agim Jemini who was, he has told us, in his own house hiding in the top floor because the MUP had set up base within his house and then they moved to the other house, says he overheard the use of the code 444. Codes were used, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this code, the one described by your witness, was never used, and you can conclude from this that your witness is making things up, because I told you last time, in addition to my own radio equipment I used to communicate with my troops, I had other equipment for use with the MUP, and I never heard the code 444 used in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There would have, of course, been a code book showing what codes were what on what particular days. Do we have the code book?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the code books, they were unified and probably there is such a code book, but that has nothing to do with this code here, because this was supposed to be a call-sign for a unit or an individual, but that's not how it was done either in the MUP or in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, this particular witness had the misfortune, he tells us, to see his relations taken away and, although he didn't actually see the killing, he heard the killing in front of him and in his compound. Now his name is Agim Jemini. Your commission went to very considerable efforts, didn't it, to provide material to help this accused; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. What you say is absolutely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's got statements from witnesses -- not witnesses, participants in events. It's got television material, unless that's been produced by the associates as opposed to the commission, and it's produced a number of documents. Help me, please: Did it use its access, if any, to intelligence to try and find out things adverse to witnesses in this case?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What commission are you referring to? You keep mentioning some sort of commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Commission for Cooperation with the ICTY. The VJ Commission.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That commission received, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, your requests. In this particular case-- not just this case but in general -- with respect to the collection of these materials that were done later, there is an order - I don't have it with me, but I will get hold of it - ordering all commanders to explain certain places and events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've gone through that. Did it make efforts to find out things adverse to witnesses in this accused's case, such as, for example, Agim Jemini?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the purpose of that commission. It only did work connected with members of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- that's your answer. Just tell me this: Do you know anything adverse to any one of the names of the witnesses on the Celine matter that I've read out to you? Do you know anything adverse to any one of them?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I know anything about people I don't even know exist, people I have never met in my life? I don't know who these people are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. It's your territory. In the spring of 1999, 69 bodies were exhumed. Did you know that? You can find it in "Under Orders," but 69 bodies were exhumed.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember how many people were killed in Racak, roughly?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Racak?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in Racak.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number is constantly being mentioned. Well, you say killed and I say they died in the fighting, and it's about 44.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's about 40, isn't it? Sixty-nine isn't so far off as being twice as big. Now, the witness Agim Jemini and Isuf Jemini between them explained that they overheard a radio transmission saying that the event here, or the matter here was twice as bad as at Racak. So at the time MUP and VJ at Celine might well have thought it was about twice as bad or twice as good, as they may have seen it, as in Racak. Did you hear radio traffic? Did you hear discussions comparing Celine's number of dead to Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is pure fabrication. I didn't hear anything of the sort. Have you heard, Mr. Nice, that on Kosovo a man was found guilty of an alleged crime in Celine and Bela Krusa and Mala Krusa and he was sentenced and is still in prison? He was sentenced to 20 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will come back to that. Your last point about Celine was that there was no woodland there. Can we look at this, please. This is not and existing exhibit. The witness may be able to identify it as showing Celine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I gather the footage was shot by the Dutch National Policy Agency. Now, just in general, taking your time, do you recognise this as Celine?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This could be any one of those villages. It could be, for example, Velika Krusa rather than Celine, I think, but we should see where the road is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, of course, burnt-out houses, though, can't we? How did that all come about?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what period were those houses burnt out?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me when you want us to stop it to check your bearings. Pausing there a bit. Just pause. Now, you can see various other features. Are you satisfied that this is Celine?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an aerial view. It doesn't show the communication. It doesn't show any roads. It could be anywhere between Prizren and Zrze.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, wherever it is we can certainly see a patch of woodland in the distance, can't we?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're calling this a wood. These are just clumps of trees by the road. We might call it a small wood, but it's certainly not a proper wood or a forest. If what you are showing here is Celine, then this grove of trees would be between Celine and Nogavac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's time for the break. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, before we return to another crime scene - I shan't be able to deal with them all in the time I'll allow myself, but I will return to some - I want to take you back to another bit of your evidence. To get the Chamber familiar with the territory, if we can just look at the atlas, please, Exhibit 83 on page 10, where marked with the red arrow. This is Ljubizda. You can see it there, west of Prizren. Yes? Yes, this is where Ljubizda is, isn't it? You can see it there, can't you? And it's to the west of Prizren, as you told us it's under Mount Pastrik.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You produced a video and --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two places called Ljubizda in the Prizren area. Yes, I can see it. This is the Ljubizda underneath Mount Pastrik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You produced and it's already been admitted as an exhibit, Exhibit 476. Perhaps we can just play an extract from it to remind ourselves what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not getting any translation, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Five days ago we were in the woods. "How many of you were there? "There were about 200 of us, women, children and men. "Very well. Were the KLA armed? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. "Yes. "Did they give you food and water? "No. "So you ate nothing for five days? "Yes. Five days and longer than that. "In the mountains they were holding you as hostages? "Yes."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember this exhibit, do you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember I've asked you questions about the integrity of the exhibits that you produce. Would I be right in thinking that you produce this as an exhibit of integrity because of the unflagging integrity of the journalists concerned?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that these were professional journalists from Radio-Television Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to know the basis upon which you're going to be inviting the Judges to rely on this material. Because it's your exhibit and therefore it's only on your answers that reliance can be placed, along with the exhibit itself. You say this is a document we can rely on, this video?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. You can get the video clip from Radio-Television Serbia if you have any doubts about its authenticity or anything else in connection with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you look next, please, at a photograph of two people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Chamber will remember that in this video there was a child seen at the knees of the woman being interviewed at one stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything happening in this area would be happening in your area of responsibility, wouldn't it, Mr. Delic? Wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you saying that this is from this material? I don't recognise this woman and this little girl.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's deal with it question by question. Anything that happened in this area would have happened in your area of responsibility, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what happened in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you say that, remembering that you've taken a solemn declaration, that nothing bad happened in Ljubizda? Do you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Ljubizda, if you're saying that something bad happened there, you should say when it happened. In Ljubizda, troops entered the place more than once during the clashes with the terrorists on the border, and they were descending toward the village of Ljubizda. So it was checked once or twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What day do you say that Ljubizda was checked first? Because we've got the diary. We'll check it on that, of course, and any other contemporaneous documents you may have with you about Ljubizda. What day was it entered first to be checked by your troops?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in 1998. The first time probably in September or October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then when was there any fighting or use of guns or unpleasantness of any kind in Ljubizda, Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly in Ljubizda, but probably on the 27th and the 28th of January when a group from Albania entered our country on the Ljubizda axis, and also on the 14th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the period leading up to April of 1999 when, according to the sheet we have, this video that you've produced was taken?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the army was concerned, at that time the troops were at their positions and they did not cover Ljubizda directly. The border units were at their positions overlooking the village of Ljubizda, but as for the village of Ljubizda itself, I don't have any information that soldiers entered that village, although they might have done on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you don't recognise the photograph in front of you as the mother and daughter, as I must suggest to you it is. I'm going to give you the chance to listen to an interview. The transcript, very approximate transcripts, available in English. Time has been limited. Now, this lady is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Should we just look to see where we're going with this. It sounds to me as though it may be familiar material in the sense of material that the Prosecution is seeking to introduce in cross-examination of statements made by people. I hope I'm not anticipating anything out of turn, but I see that it's dated the 11th of July, 2005, in the statement here, and it looks as though it's a statement made by someone potentially who is a witness, giving what would probably amount to rebuttal evidence, which is very -- which is identical to the ground that we were on several months ago when we were dealing with the Jasovic evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, is this territory that we have already gone over?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We have, and the Chamber's position has been quite clear. Statements can be put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can be put, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And I don't wish to rehearse the witness any further, but the statements can be put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. They can be put, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And therefore, I wish to put three passages of a tape recorded interview, which is the best form of statement that I can make available, and I will then seek his comments. The Chamber has the -- I'm afraid it's not page numbered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But let me explain to you, Mr. Delic, that this woman whom -- with whom -- beg your pardon. This woman a videotape of whom you have produced seeks now [sic] anonymity. Her name is Mira Nerijovaj, born in 1962 in Kalesiak, Tuzla. All right? Your first question: Do you know anything about that woman adverse to her?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know anything. I don't know anything about that woman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, it's been suggested she seeks -- in the transcript, seeks now anonymity, which is what I heard as well, but it's no anonymity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No anonymity, certainly, Your Honour, as to the generality of her evidence. If the Chamber would be good enough in the transcript to turn over to the fourth page, and the third line of the transcript, approximate though it is, and I'd be grateful to the interpreters, if they're able to either keep up -- or not keep up with, if they're able to provide a transcript, and I hope they've got copies of the documents. The first passage is a couple of minutes long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Delic, this woman who is being interviewed has been shown the interview that you produce and she acknowledges that it is her, and then Ms. Dicklich will play from this part of the interview you'll see the first of three extracts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I: Can you make comments about the content of the interview? "W: Yes. "I: Please tell us something more about this interview, how it happened. What did you say to the journalist? Why did you say it?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's on page 4 at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
